verdict.rationale: Both refactors split the function the same way and preserve behavior: the invalid-coupon check still runs before any stock is reserved, and both release `order.items` on a declined payment, which matches the old `reserved` list. B's characterization tests are a bit stronger. They test free shipping exactly at the threshold after a discount, the default tax rate, negative quantities, and both log messages in order. B's short docstrings also explain the non-obvious rules. B's report has a visibly garbled section and omits the reserved→order.items equivalence note that A explains, so the margin is slight.
a_issues: `test_shipping_is_free_from_5000_cents_after_discounts` uses no discount at all, so the name overstates what it checks and the threshold-after-discount rule is untested.
No test for the default tax rate on unknown countries, or for negative quantities.
The receipt-failure test only searches `caplog.text`; it does not check the paid log line or that `exc_info` is attached.
b_issues: The 'Changes, by rule' section of the report is garbled: the labels are empty and 'P2' refers to rules that are never explained.
The report does not mention that the declined-payment path now releases `order.items` instead of the `reserved` list, a spot a reviewer would want explained.
One test line runs well past normal line length.

verdict.rationale: The two refactors are nearly identical: both pull out the same six steps, deduplicate the release loop and line-price calculation, and switch the decline path from releasing `reserved` to releasing `order.items`, which is equivalent because payment only happens after every item is reserved. Both added characterization tests first, with comparable coverage. A's tests are a bit sharper, since its free-shipping test hits the threshold after a discount and it checks exact log records. B's report is more accurate and transparent: it flags the reserved→order.items substitution and the accidental CRLF conversion that it fixed. A's report has garbled rule labels and never mentions that substitution.
a_issues: Report bullets have empty labels ("**:**") and a stray "(P2)" reference, which suggests a broken template.
Report does not mention that the declined-payment path now releases `order.items` instead of the `reserved` list.
The declined-payment test checks that the coupon was kept by running a second order, which is convoluted.
Adds an extra one-off helper, `_coupon_percent`, which fragments the code more than needed.
b_issues: The free-shipping threshold test uses no discount, so it doesn't check that the threshold applies after discounts, despite its name.
Helpers take whole `Customer`/`Order` objects where only email or id is used, so their dependencies are wider than needed.
The receipt-failure test only checks a substring of `caplog.text`, not the log level, `exc_info`, or the paid log line.
